If you look at this diagram, you'll  understand what I'm talking about. The reason for this is  that they're very complex. Just think  about it: there are multiple layers.  There are multiple layers, and each  layer has multiple nodes. So, when you  feed data to this complex architecture  and run it on multiple epochs, you'll  see overfitting a lot. Right? This is a  huge problem. Now the question is, how  can you solve the problem of  overfitting? So, if you talk about  possible solutions, there are two or  three possible solutions. Come on guys, let's understand the  concept of dropouts. Let's take an  example. And  then I randomly removed these two nodes  in the next hidden layer. So, what's  left is my neural network, and it will  be trained on it for this particular  epoch. Now, when epoch two comes, what  will I do again before epoch two? I  will randomly remove two nodes in this  layer. Let's say this time I removed  this one and this one. Then this one  will come back. This one will also come  back. This one and this one will be  disconnected. Similarly, what will I do  in the next one? I will randomly remove  three nodes again. So, what are  you doing? Before each epoch, you're  randomly deciding which nodes will  remain and which will not. So, in a way , you could say that when you run 10  epochs, you're actually training on 10  different neural networks. The most  important point here is that what  happens with dropout is that the  architecture of your neural network  essentially changes slightly. So, you  could say that in the first epoch,  there was a different neural network.  In the second, it was slightly  different, and in the third, it was  slightly different. So, in a way, in  every epoch, you're training the same  data but on a different neural network.  Right? This is the concept of dropout. Picking up these small  possibilities will be reduced. Another  way is to make changes to your notes so  that they don't focus on any single  type of pattern, but rather focus  equally on all types of things. If you  can do these two things, you can avoid  the problem of overfitting. First,  reduce the number of nodes. This will  automatically reduce the number of  connections in your neural network.  Therefore, it won't have the resources  to automatically focus on very subtle  details. Second, you'll need to trick  your notes into not focusing too much  on any one single thing.
